NKJV.1: Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
NKJV.2: And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her and lay with her, and violated her.
NKJV.3: His soul was strongly attracted to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young woman and spoke kindly to the young woman.
NKJV.4: So Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, “Get me this young woman as a wife.”
NKJV.5: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter. Now his sons were with his livestock in the field; so Jacob held his peace until they came.
NKJV.6: Then Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.
NKJV.7: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it; and the men were grieved and very angry, because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter, a thing which ought not to be done.
NKJV.8: But Hamor spoke with them, saying, “The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
NKJV.9: And make marriages with us; give your daughters to us, and take our daughters to yourselves.
NKJV.10: So you shall dwell with us, and the land shall be before you. Dwell and trade in it, and acquire possessions for yourselves in it.”
NKJV.11: Then Shechem said to her father and her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will give.
NKJV.12: Ask me ever so much dowry and gift, and I will give according to what you say to me; but give me the young woman as a wife.”
NKJV.13: But the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father, and spoke deceitfully, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
NKJV.14: And they said to them, “We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised, for that would be a reproach to us.
NKJV.15: But on this condition we will consent to you: If you will become as we are, if every male of you is circumcised,
NKJV.16: then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to us; and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
NKJV.17: But if you will not heed us and be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and be gone.”
NKJV.18: And their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.
NKJV.19: So the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in Jacob’s daughter. He was more honorable than all the household of his father.
NKJV.20: And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke with the men of their city, saying:
NKJV.21: “These men are at peace with us. Therefore let them dwell in the land and trade in it. For indeed the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters to us as wives, and let us give them our daughters.
NKJV.22: Only on this condition will the men consent to dwell with us, to be one people: if every male among us is circumcised as they are circumcised.
NKJV.23: Will not their livestock, their property, and every animal of theirs be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”
NKJV.24: And all who went out of the gate of his city heeded Hamor and Shechem his son; every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
NKJV.25: Now it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword and came boldly upon the city and killed all the males.
NKJV.26: And they killed Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem’s house, and went out.
NKJV.27: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because their sister had been defiled.
NKJV.28: They took their sheep, their oxen, and their donkeys, what was in the city and what was in the field,
NKJV.29: and all their wealth. All their little ones and their wives they took captive; and they plundered even all that was in the houses.
NKJV.30: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me by making me obnoxious among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites; and since I am few in number, they will gather themselves together against me and kill me. I shall be destroyed, my household and I.”
NKJV.31: But they said, “Should he treat our sister like a harlot?”

NASB.1: Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the daughters of the land.

NASB.3: He was deeply attracted to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the girl and spoke tenderly to her.
NASB.4: So Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, 'Get me this young girl for a wife.'
NASB.5: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter; but his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob kept silent until they came in.
NASB.6: Then Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.
NASB.7: Now the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard [it]; and the men were grieved, and they were very angry because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter, for such a thing ought not to be done.
NASB.8: But Hamor spoke with them, saying, 'The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter; please give her to him in marriage.
NASB.9: 'Intermarry with us; give your daughters to us and take our daughters for yourselves.
NASB.10: 'Thus you shall live with us, and the land shall be [open] before you; live and trade in it and acquire property in it.'
NASB.11: Shechem also said to her father and to her brothers, 'If I find favor in your sight, then I will give whatever you say to me.
NASB.12: 'Ask me ever so much bridal payment and gift, and I will give according as you say to me; but give me the girl in marriage.'
NASB.13: But Jacob's sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor with deceit, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
NASB.14: They said to them, 'We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised, for that would be a disgrace to us.
NASB.15: 'Only on this [condition] will we consent to you: if you will become like us, in that every male of you be circumcised,
NASB.16: then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters for ourselves, and we will live with you and become one people.
NASB.17: 'But if you will not listen to us to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and go.'
NASB.18: Now their words seemed reasonable to Hamor and Shechem, Hamor's son.
NASB.19: The young man did not delay to do the thing, because he was delighted with Jacob's daughter. Now he was more respected than all the household of his father.

NASB.22: 'Only on this [condition] will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people: that every male among us be circumcised as they are circumcised.
NASB.23: 'Will not their livestock and their property and all their animals be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will live with us.'
NASB.24: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and to his son Shechem, and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
NASB.25: Now it came about on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, each took his sword and came upon the city unawares, and killed every male.
NASB.26: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem's house, and went forth.
NASB.27: Jacob's sons came upon the slain and looted the city, because they had defiled their sister.
NASB.28: They took their flocks and their herds and their donkeys, and that which was in the city and that which was in the field;
NASB.29: and they captured and looted all their wealth and all their little ones and their wives, even all that [was] in the houses.
NASB.30: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, 'You have brought trouble on me by making me odious among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites; and my men being few in number, they will gather together against me and attack me and I will be destroyed, I and my household.'

ESV.1: Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the women of the land.
ESV.2: And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her, he seized her and lay with her and humiliated her.
ESV.3: And his soul was drawn to Dinah the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her.
ESV.4: So Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, “Get me this girl for my wife.”
ESV.5: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled his daughter Dinah. But his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob held his peace until they came.
ESV.6: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.
ESV.7: The sons of Jacob had come in from the field as soon as they heard of it, and the men were indignant and very angry, because he had done an outrageous thing in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter, for such a thing must not be done.
ESV.8: But Hamor spoke with them, saying, “The soul of my son Shechem longs for your  daughter. Please give her to him to be his wife.
ESV.9: Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
ESV.10: You shall dwell with us, and the land shall be open to you. Dwell and trade in it, and get property in it.”
ESV.11: Shechem also said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will give.
ESV.12: Ask me for as great a bride-price  and gift as you will, and I will give whatever you say to me. Only give me the young woman to be my wife.”
ESV.13: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and his father Hamor deceitfully, because he had defiled their sister Dinah.
ESV.14: They said to them, “We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised, for that would be a disgrace to us.
ESV.15: Only on this condition will we agree with you — that you will become as we are by every male among you being circumcised.
ESV.16: Then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to ourselves, and we will dwell with you and become one people.
ESV.17: But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, then we will take our daughter, and we will be gone.”
ESV.18: Their words pleased Hamor and Hamor's son Shechem.
ESV.19: And the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in Jacob's daughter. Now he was the most honored of all his father's house.
ESV.20: So Hamor and his son Shechem came to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of their city, saying,
ESV.21: “These men are at peace with us; let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for behold, the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters as wives, and let us give them our daughters.
ESV.22: Only on this condition will the men agree to dwell with us to become one people — when every male among us is circumcised as they are circumcised.
ESV.23: Will not their livestock, their property and all their beasts be ours? Only let us agree with them, and they will dwell with us.”
ESV.24: And all who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
ESV.25: On the third day, when they were sore, two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords and came against the city while it felt secure and killed all the males.
ESV.26: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the sword and took Dinah out of Shechem's house and went away.
ESV.27: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
ESV.28: They took their flocks and their herds, their donkeys, and whatever was in the city and in the field.
ESV.29: All their wealth, all their little ones and their wives, all that was in the houses, they captured and plundered.
ESV.30: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble on me by making me stink to the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. My numbers are few, and if they gather themselves against me and attack me, I shall be destroyed, both I and my household.”
ESV.31: But they said, “Should he treat our sister like a prostitute?”

NLT.1: One day Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the young women who lived in the area.
NLT.2: But when the local prince, Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, saw Dinah, he seized her and raped her.
NLT.3: But then he fell in love with her, and he tried to win her affection with tender words.
NLT.4: He said to his father, Hamor, “Get me this young girl. I want to marry her.”
NLT.5: Soon Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter, Dinah. But since his sons were out in the fields herding his livestock, he said nothing until they returned.
NLT.6: Hamor, Shechem’s father, came to discuss the matter with Jacob.
NLT.7: Meanwhile, Jacob’s sons had come in from the field as soon as they heard what had happened. They were shocked and furious that their sister had been raped. Shechem had done a disgraceful thing against Jacob’s family, something that should never be done.
NLT.8: Hamor tried to speak with Jacob and his sons. “My son Shechem is truly in love with your daughter,” he said. “Please let him marry her.
NLT.9: In fact, let’s arrange other marriages, too. You give us your daughters for our sons, and we will give you our daughters for your sons.
NLT.10: And you may live among us; the land is open to you! Settle here and trade with us. And feel free to buy property in the area.”
NLT.11: Then Shechem himself spoke to Dinah’s father and brothers. “Please be kind to me, and let me marry her,” he begged. “I will give you whatever you ask.
NLT.12: No matter what dowry or gift you demand, I will gladly pay it — just give me the girl as my wife.”
NLT.13: But since Shechem had defiled their sister, Dinah, Jacob’s sons responded deceitfully to Shechem and his father, Hamor.
NLT.14: They said to them, “We couldn’t possibly allow this, because you’re not circumcised. It would be a disgrace for our sister to marry a man like you!
NLT.15: But here is a solution. If every man among you will be circumcised like we are,
NLT.16: then we will give you our daughters, and we’ll take your daughters for ourselves. We will live among you and become one people.
NLT.17: But if you don’t agree to be circumcised, we will take her and be on our way.”
NLT.18: Hamor and his son Shechem agreed to their proposal.
NLT.19: Shechem wasted no time in acting on this request, for he wanted Jacob’s daughter desperately. Shechem was a highly respected member of his family,
NLT.20: and he went with his father, Hamor, to present this proposal to the leaders at the town gate.
NLT.21: “These men are our friends,” they said. “Let’s invite them to live here among us and trade freely. Look, the land is large enough to hold them. We can take their daughters as wives and let them marry ours.
NLT.22: But they will consider staying here and becoming one people with us only if all of our men are circumcised, just as they are.
NLT.23: But if we do this, all their livestock and possessions will eventually be ours. Come, let’s agree to their terms and let them settle here among us.”
NLT.24: So all the men in the town council agreed with Hamor and Shechem, and every male in the town was circumcised.
NLT.25: But three days later, when their wounds were still sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, who were Dinah’s full brothers, took their swords and entered the town without opposition. Then they slaughtered every male there,
NLT.26: including Hamor and his son Shechem. They killed them with their swords, then took Dinah from Shechem’s house and returned to their camp.
NLT.27: Meanwhile, the rest of Jacob’s sons arrived. Finding the men slaughtered, they plundered the town because their sister had been defiled there.
NLT.28: They seized all the flocks and herds and donkeys — everything they could lay their hands on, both inside the town and outside in the fields.
NLT.29: They looted all their wealth and plundered their houses. They also took all their little children and wives and led them away as captives.
NLT.30: Afterward Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have ruined me! You’ve made me stink among all the people of this land — among all the Canaanites and Perizzites. We are so few that they will join forces and crush us. I will be ruined, and my entire household will be wiped out!”

MSG.23: This is a very good deal for us—these people are very wealthy with great herds of livestock and we're going to get our hands on it. So let's do what they ask and have them settle down with us."
MSG.24: Everyone who was anyone in the city agreed with Hamor and his son, Shechem; every male was circumcised.
MSG.25: Three days after the circumcision, while all the men were still very sore, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, each with his sword in hand, walked into the city as if they owned the place and murdered every man there.
MSG.26: They also killed Hamor and his son Shechem, rescued Dinah from Shechem's house, and left.
MSG.27: When the rest of Jacob's sons came on the scene of slaughter, they looted the entire city in retaliation for Dinah's rape.
MSG.28: Flocks, herds, donkeys, belongings—everything, whether in the city or the fields—they took.
MSG.29: And then they took all the wives and children captive and ransacked their homes for anything valuable.
MSG.30: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You've made my name stink to high heaven among the people here, these Canaanites and Perizzites. If they decided to gang up on us and attack, as few as we are we wouldn't stand a chance; they'd wipe me and my people right off the map."
MSG.31: They said, "Nobody is going to treat our sister like a whore and get by with it."
